title: Bank of England MPC decision (no report) — the first committee to see the electricity-VAT reversion in a published print, seven weeks after the MPR that had to forecast it
source: EST: bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the page's '2027 provisional dates' block lists 'Thursday 4 February' (February MPC Summary and minutes and February Monetary Policy Report), 'Thursday 18 March', 'Thursday 29 April' (with April MPR), 'Thursday 17 June', 'Thursday 29 July' (with July MPR), 'Thursday 16 September', 'Thursday 4 November' (with November MPR) and 'Thursday 16 December'. This entry is the 17 June announcement, which carries minutes but NO Monetary Policy Report. The Bank labels its 2027 dates PROVISIONAL, which is the honest reason for `estimate` on top of the standing schema gap: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:) has no slot for a non-US central bank. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-cpi-2027-05-19, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-cpi-2027-05-19 LANE, 2026-09-09, to close a sequencing gap the uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01 lane NAMED IN PROSE but did not diarise: it proposed boe-decision-2027-04-29 (the MPR that must forecast the reversion blind) and left the meeting that actually SEES the print unowned. Laid against the ONS release calendar (fetched the same day) the order is: MPC 2027-03-18 (no report, pre-lapse) -> the lapse 2027-04-01 -> March 2027 CPI 2027-04-21 (still drag-in, the last pre-reversion read) -> MPC + MPR 2027-04-29, which must publish a forecast EMBEDDING the reversion with NO post-lapse data -> April 2027 CPI 2027-05-19, the first observation -> THIS MEETING, the first committee to have it. Forecast and observation are SEVEN WEEKS apart. THE INFERENCE, AND IT IS A LOOK-THROUGH ARGUMENT NOT A RATE CALL: the same structure occurred on the way down (the November 2026 MPR embedded the cut; the October print landed after the 2026-11-05 vote), and a self-reversing tax notch whose forecast and observation never coincide is exactly what a committee looks through. It moves printed numbers; it is materially weaker evidence about the rate path than its headline size suggests. WHAT MAKES THIS MEETING THE INTERESTING ONE RATHER THAN A FORMALITY: it is the first venue where the April MPR's forecast of the step can be checked against the realised print, and the proposing lane's own finding is that the realised print WILL NOT SETTLE IT AT THE HEADLINE -- the April year-on-year step versus March has averaged 0.594pp absolute across 2010-2026 (ONS D7G7, n=17) and all seventeen exceeded the roughly 0.098pp VAT effect, so a committee reading the headline alone cannot see whether its own forecast of the notch was right. The separable venue is the electricity index against the gas index (04.5.1 vs 04.5.2; gas shares the Ofgem cap and kept its 5% VAT), registered as FT-uk-cpi-2027-05-19-1. NO DIRECTIONAL VIEW ON BANK RATE IS REGISTERED HERE -- the proposing lane researched a CPI print's readability, not UK monetary policy, and has no MPC forward test. Tiered LOW: symbols: [], and this calendar's entire tracked universe is eight US mega-caps with no UK listing, gilt or sterling instrument; the only transmission channel this repo has ever measured is the gilt-to-Treasury pipe quantified in uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28, which opens only on the worst roughly 1% of gilt days. Estimate widens caution only; the Bank's own 2027 dates are provisional and should be re-checked against its published calendar before anything is keyed to them.
